The election was on the same day as other [[2026 United Kingdom local elections|local elections across England]]. All seats were contested;{{Cite web |title=Election timetable in England |url=https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/election-timetable-in-england/election-timetable-in-england |access-date=2024-04-07 |website=GOV.UK |language=en}} this was the first all-out election since 2012.{{Cite web |last=Lennon |first=Marie |date=2026-04-09 |title=Why Swindon's first all-out election in more than a decade matters |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cj0ved50qjqo |access-date=2026-04-11 |website=BBC News |language=en-GB}} At the [[2024 Swindon Borough Council election|previous council election]], [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour]] kept overall majority control of the council with 41 out of 57 seats, with the Conservatives having 15 seats.{{cite news |last1=Thomas |first1=Aled |title=Labour tightens grip on Swindon council after election triumph |url=https://www.swindonadvertiser.co.uk/news/24297849.labour-tightens-grip-swindon-council-election-triumph/ |access-date=22 July 2024 |work=Swindon Advertiser |date=3 May 2024}} In 2025, four Labour councillors defected to the [[Green Party of England and Wales|Green Party]].{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c1lrng1qn92o|website=BBC News|title=Town sees fourth councillor defect to Greens|last=Robertson|date=26 November 2025|first=Kirsten|accessdate=15 December 2025}} ==Previous council composition== {| class="wikitable" |- ! colspan="3" | After 2024 election ! colspan="3" | Before 2026 election ! rowspan="2" |Change |- ! colspan="2" | Party !
